options.C: Because they are legally banned from ever learning about health
options.D: Because they miss out on health education delivered strictly inside classrooms

explanation: Adolescents who have dropped out of school or never attended miss school-based programs, so community initiatives are their primary lifeline. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks gestation received her first dose of IPTp-SP four weeks ago. What is the correct clinical action for today's visit?

options.A: Withhold SP until she reaches 36 weeks of pregnancy
options.B: Refer her to the laboratory for a rapid diagnostic malaria test first
options.C: Administer her second dose of IPTp-SP under direct observation
options.D: Prescribe a double dose to make up for missed weeks in the first trimester

explanation: Doses of SP are given at least one month apart throughout the second and third trimesters until delivery, so she is due for her next dose. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h5)

question: A midwife wants to type an official memo for the maternity ward. Which type of software should she open?

options.A: System utility software
options.B: Application software
options.C: Device driver software
options.D: Firmware update software

explanation: Word processors and document creators are application software used directly for writing tasks like memos and reports. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T3#BMP123_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the very first thing that forms inside a fresh bone break within the first few days?

options.A: A thick layer of scar skin
options.B: A permanent steel plate
options.C: A blood clot hematoma
options.D: A hard compact shell

explanation: Blood vessels break during a fracture, and the resulting bleeding pools around the ends to form an initial protective hematoma. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which joint is the only direct bone connection between the arm and the rest of the skeleton?

options.A: Sternoclavicular joint
options.B: Scapulothoracic joint
options.C: Acromioclavicular joint
options.D: Glenohumeral joint

explanation: The sternoclavicular joint connects the entire shoulder girdle and arm to the sternum. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T10#BMP111_U2_T10_h3)

question: Where is pain typically felt during a gallbladder attack (biliary colic)?

options.A: Right upper abdomen radiating to the right shoulder
options.B: Lower belly area radiating down both legs
options.C: Lower left abdomen radiating to the groin
options.D: Left upper abdomen radiating to the chest

explanation: Irritation of nearby nerves by an inflamed or blocked gallbladder often causes pain that travels to the right shoulder or upper back. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T5#BMP125_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of progesterone during most of the pregnancy?

options.A: Stimulating regular uterine contractions
options.B: Keeping the uterine muscle relaxed and quiet
options.C: Increasing the blood pressure of the mother
options.D: Softening and opening up the cervix early

explanation: Progesterone acts as a natural relaxant for the uterus, preventing early birth until its levels drop at term. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the most important rule for a midwife when caring for mothers in labor?

options.A: Dignity and respect without discrimination
options.B: Strict adherence to hospital financial quotas
options.C: Limiting patient movement during early labor
options.D: Prioritizing the doctor over the patient always

explanation: Every client has a human right to receive fair and equal care, no matter their background or status. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T2#BMP310_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does the maternal cardiovascular system undergo such massive changes during pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent the mother from developing high blood pressure
options.B: To shrink the size of the maternal kidneys and liver
options.C: To supply enough oxygen and nutrients to the growing fetus
options.D: To prepare the mother for heavy manual labor after delivery

explanation: The entire remodeling process exists to ensure the placenta receives enough blood flow to nourish and oxygenate the baby safely. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T4#BMP212_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of selective toxicity when using antimicrobial drugs?

options.A: Preventing the drug from dissolving too quickly
options.B: Boosting the patient's natural immune system response
options.C: Broadening the range of bacteria the drug kills
options.D: Destroying the pathogen without harming host cells

explanation: Selective toxicity means the medication targets and kills the invading germ while keeping the mother's or baby's own cells safe from harm. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of Community-Based IMCI (C-IMCI)?

options.A: Training mothers to perform surgical procedures at home
options.B: Eliminating the need for facility-based health workers
options.C: Replacing primary health centers with mobile surgical vans
options.D: Extending life-saving child health interventions directly into villages and homes

explanation: C-IMCI takes health education and basic care out of the clinic and into the community where families live. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h7)

question: Where should paper questionnaires be kept once data collection is finished?

options.A: In locked filing cabinets
options.B: In public community halls
options.C: Inside personal handbags
options.D: On open clinic waiting benches

explanation: Physical documents containing personal and health information must be kept in secure, locked storage to protect participant confidentiality. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T4#BMP225_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of carrying out a community diagnosis in midwifery?

options.A: To provide free drugs to every household in the district
options.B: To replace the national census figures with local estimates
options.C: To identify local health problems and available community resources
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet hospital targets

explanation: A community diagnosis helps find out what health challenges exist locally and what resources are already available to support care. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which dietary mineral is usually restricted for patients experiencing significant swelling and fluid retention?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Magnesium

explanation: Restricting salt (sodium) helps the body hold onto less water, making it easier for diuretic drugs to reduce swelling. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which Boolean operator should you use when you want to broaden your search to include synonyms?

options.A: NOT
options.B: OR
options.C: WITH
options.D: AND

explanation: The OR operator tells the database to find articles containing at least one of the listed terms, increasing the number of results. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h3)

question: A female client is treated for a sexually transmitted infection at the PHC. Why must her sexual partner be treated too?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory administrative paperwork required by the local government
options.B: To prevent reinfection and break the cycle of disease transmission within the community
options.C: To ensure the couple does not experience psychological stress from mistrust
options.D: Because men are legally responsible for all medical bills incurred by their spouses

explanation: Treating partners at the same time stops infections from being passed back and forth between them. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T8#BMP126_U2_T8_h6)

question: What physical sensation triggers the Moro reflex in a newborn?

options.A: A sudden feeling of falling or loss of support
options.B: A sharp pinch on the bottom of the foot
options.C: A loud scratching sound near the ear
options.D: A bright flash of light shining in the eyes

explanation: The Moro reflex specifically responds to an abrupt change in equilibrium, mimicking a fall or sudden drop in support. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T3#BMP214_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is giving Syntometrine directly into a vein (IV bolus) discouraged?

options.A: It takes over thirty minutes to produce any noticeable clinical effect
options.B: It can cause a dangerous and sudden spike in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: It completely stops the oxytocin from working on the uterine muscle fibers
options.D: It causes the placenta to detach before the baby's head is even born

explanation: An intravenous injection of ergometrine causes blood vessels to narrow too quickly, leading to a dangerous spike in blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: An institution gets an unexpectedly large number of student midwives for a new semester. What is the most practical way to teach core theory right away?

options.A: Suspending all theoretical classes until smaller rooms are built
options.B: Delivering a well-structured lecture to the combined cohort
options.C: Assigning every student a separate online research topic
options.D: Dividing students into pairs for independent hospital shifts

explanation: When class sizes suddenly increase, lecturing is the most practical way to cover baseline material efficiently without needing extra teachers. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h3)

question: A first-time mother just delivered a healthy baby, but her uterus feels soft and boggy, resulting in steady bleeding. What is the appropriate immediate medication action?

options.A: Giving a high dose of ergometrine to help push out the remaining placenta
options.B: Administering ergometrine to stimulate firm uterine contractions
options.C: Waiting for one hour to see if the uterus hardens on its own
options.D: Starting an oral tablet of ergometrine to speed up cervical dilation

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus indicates uterine atony, which requires a potent uterotonic like ergometrine to force contraction. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T2#BMP213_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for elevating a newly casted limb above heart level?

options.A: To stop the bone from growing too fast
options.B: To prevent swelling and fluid buildup
options.C: To help the plaster dry within minutes
options.D: To make the skin change color safely

explanation: Elevation uses gravity to drain excess fluid away from the injury site, reducing swelling that could otherwise cause dangerous pressure inside the rigid cast. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why does the nurse change their role from substitutive to complementary as the patient recovers?

options.A: To support the patient's increasing independence and ability to self-care
options.B: To shift all responsibilities entirely back to the patient's family members
options.C: To reduce the number of nursing hours billed to the hospital ward
options.D: To comply strictly with changing medical doctor prescriptions

explanation: As patients regain strength, the nurse steps back from doing everything for them to partnering with them as they resume control. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T7#BMP110_U3_T7_h4)

question: What happens to contractions during disordered uterine action?

options.A: The umbilical cord drops below the presenting part of the fetus
options.B: Contractions deviate from the normal rhythmic and coordinated pattern
options.C: Amniotic fluid turns green due to early meconium passage
options.D: The placenta separates prematurely before the second stage

explanation: Disordered uterine action means the womb's contractions lose their usual smooth rhythm and teamwork. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T2#BMP311_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which specific cells inside the testes make testosterone?

options.A: Spermatogonia stem cells
options.B: Sertoli nurse cells
options.C: Interstitial cells of Leydig
options.D: Primary spermatocytes

explanation: The Leydig cells are found in the tissue between the seminiferous tubules and are responsible for secreting testosterone. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T2#BMP210_U3_T2_h2)

question: How do anaesthetic drugs primarily cross over from the mother to the fetus?

options.A: Direct injection into the umbilical cord
options.B: Simple diffusion across the placenta
options.C: Active transport via fetal red blood cells
options.D: Swallowing through the amniotic fluid

explanation: Most small molecular drugs easily cross the placental barrier and enter the fetal circulation. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T5#BMP124_U3_T5_h5)

question: A patient wants an implant but is scared because her mother-in-law says contraceptives rot inside the womb. How should the midwife reply?

options.A: Tell the client to ignore her mother-in-law completely and get the implant in secret
options.B: Refuse to provide any family planning until the entire extended family attends clinic
options.C: Agree with the mother-in-law's warning and suggest traditional herbs instead
options.D: Provide clear, respectful education that debunks the myth and offer to speak with the family if desired

explanation: Respectful conversation bridges the gap between traditional fears and medical facts without disrespecting the patient's family support system. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common clinical use of virtual meetings in midwifery?

options.A: Running group antenatal education classes
options.B: Conducting virtual postnatal check-ups
options.C: Performing major surgical abdominal operations
options.D: Holding emergency multidisciplinary case reviews

explanation: Virtual meetings facilitate communication and observation, but physical surgery requires hands-on presence. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h3)

question: How do midwives best help stop the problem of VVF in local communities over the long term?

options.A: Enforcing strict legal penalties against traditional healers
options.B: Performing routine fistula repairs in primary health clinics
options.C: Providing financial grants to families of pregnant women
options.D: Promoting hospital delivery and proper partograph use

explanation: Using partographs to monitor labor and encouraging births in health facilities helps stop prolonged labor before a fistula can form. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why are verbal drug orders generally discouraged in routine clinical practice?

options.A: They take too long to write down later
options.B: They are easily misheard or misunderstood
options.C: Pharmacy departments refuse to supply them
options.D: They are illegal in all African countries

explanation: Spoken instructions lack a written paper trail and can be easily distorted in a noisy, busy clinical environment. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T1#BMP120_U2_T1_h5)

question: How can midwives best support mothers worried about community reactions to their baby's cleft?

options.A: Suggest hiding the facial defect with heavy blankets at all times
options.B: Advise the mother to stay strictly indoors until the baby is fully grown
options.C: Provide compassionate counseling and connect them with local support groups
options.D: Explain that societal reactions cannot be changed under any circumstances

explanation: Listening with empathy, sharing information about surgical repair, and connecting families with peer groups helps them handle social worries. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T5#BMP220_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the correct professional action to take when a midwife makes a writing error inside an antenatal record?

options.A: Leave the error uncorrected since crossing out looks untidy
options.B: Tear out the affected page and rewrite the entire record cleanly
options.C: Apply correction fluid generously and write the new text over it
options.D: Draw a single neat line through the error, write the correction, and sign

explanation: Standard documentation rules require crossing out mistakes with a single line so the original entry remains legible, followed by the correct entry and signature. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is strict confidentiality especially crucial when managing maternal mental health issues?

options.A: It prevents family members from ever visiting the postnatal ward
options.B: It stops nurses from communicating with each other during shift handovers
options.C: Hospital management requires all mental health records to be published publicly
options.D: Stigma surrounding mental illness in many communities can deter women from seeking care

explanation: Fear of judgment or gossip stops many mothers from speaking up, so guarding their privacy protects their willingness to seek help. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T6#BMP223_U4_T6_h6)

question: The local health ministry wants to know the total number of postpartum haemorrhage cases treated last month. Where should the midwife look for this information?

options.A: Staff attendance sign-in sheets
options.B: The personal diary of the head of nursing
options.C: General hospital cafeteria purchase receipts
options.D: Maternity unit registers and delivery logs

explanation: Official ward registers track diagnoses and complications systematically, making them the correct source for hospital reports. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h6)

question: A 28-week pregnant woman comes to the antenatal clinic complaining of severe backache, fever, and pain when passing urine. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: Relaxin hormone softening ligaments
options.B: An uncomplicated false labor pain
options.C: A urinary tract infection
options.D: Normal physiological weight gain

explanation: Fever and painful urination combined with back pain strongly point toward a urinary tract issue rather than simple muscle strain. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T13#BMP212_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of emergency preparedness in an antenatal ward?

options.A: Conducting regular team emergency drills for staff
options.B: Having working suction machines available at the bedside
options.C: Ensuring oxygen delivery systems are fully functional
options.D: Keeping all emergency drug trays locked away in the pharmacy

explanation: Emergency drugs must be immediately accessible right on the ward, not locked away in a distant pharmacy, during a crisis. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which medication is usually given first for Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Acarbose
options.B: Metformin
options.C: Glibenclamide
options.D: Regular insulin

explanation: Metformin is widely used first because it helps reduce sugar production in the liver and helps the body use insulin better without causing low blood sugar on its own. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T2#BMP216_U2_T2_h4)

question: What specific name is given to the fibrous ligaments that anchor a tooth inside its bony socket?

options.A: Interosseous membranes
options.B: Articular capsules
options.C: Coronal sutures
options.D: Periodontal ligaments

explanation: The periodontal ligament consists of short collagen fibers running between the tooth root and the bony socket wall to hold it in place. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T14#BMP111_U2_T14_h4)

question: A patient with hypertension asks a midwife for advice on exercising safely. What recommendation should the midwife give?

options.A: Engage in moderate physical activity like brisk walking regularly
options.B: Avoid all forms of physical movement to protect the heart
options.C: Lift heavy weights at the gym until complete exhaustion
options.D: Only exercise once a month for several hours at a time

explanation: Regular moderate exercise strengthens the cardiovascular system without placing sudden, dangerous strain on the heart. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T2#BMP125_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which large blood vessel is compressed by the uterus when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

options.A: Jugular vein
options.B: Renal artery
options.C: Carotid artery
options.D: Inferior vena cava

explanation: The heavy uterus presses directly on the inferior vena cava in the supine position, blocking blood flow back to the heart. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T4#BMP212_U1_T4_h5)

question: What effect do cholinergic drugs typically have on the pupils of the eyes?

options.A: Complete paralysis
options.B: Constriction (miosis)
options.C: Rapid blinking
options.D: Dilating very wide

explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation causes the circular muscles of the iris to contract, leading to pupil constriction known as miosis. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T4#BMP124_U2_T4_h4)

question: Where does an incisional hernia form on the body?

options.A: At the site of a previous surgical scar
options.B: Inside the upper chest cavity near the lungs
options.C: Below the inguinal ligament in the thigh
options.D: Directly through the natural navel opening

explanation: Incisional hernias appear right where a past surgery weakened the muscle or tissue layers while healing. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T8#BMP125_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why should you carefully check the newborn right after a shoulder dystocia delivery?

options.A: To prevent the development of neonatal jaundice in the first hour
options.B: To measure the exact length of the infant's arms and legs
options.C: To detect hidden fractures or nerve injuries like Erb's palsy early
options.D: To confirm the gestational age estimated during antenatal care

explanation: Checking the baby early for collarbone cracks or arm nerve issues helps ensure they get the right care right away. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T7#BMP311_U1_T7_h7)

question: A student struggles with an abdominal palpation during a bedside session. What is the best way for the instructor to handle this?

options.A: Stop teaching entirely and take over all patient care duties
options.B: Correct the technique gently while reassuring the patient and student
options.C: Scold the student loudly so other patients know standards are high
options.D: Wait until the end of the rotation weeks later to mention it

explanation: Gentle, immediate guidance protects patient confidence while helping the student learn safely. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T6#BMP312_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a main reason for getting a mother to walk around early after a caesarean section?

options.A: Speeding up the closure of the abdominal skin wound
options.B: Reducing the need for intravenous pain relief medications
options.C: Preventing deep vein thrombosis and blood clots
options.D: Ensuring immediate return of normal bowel movements

explanation: Getting the mother out of bed early improves blood circulation in the legs, lowering the risk of dangerous blood clots. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T4#BMP311_U3_T4_h5)

question: A postpartum mother complains of severe nipple pain and shows linear abrasions on her nipples. What is the most appropriate initial assessment to make?

options.A: Check the mother's temperature for signs of systemic infection
options.B: Prescribe an oral antifungal medication for suspected thrush
options.C: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding for forty-eight hours
options.D: Observe the baby's latch and positioning at the breast

explanation: Nipple pain and trauma are almost always caused by poor attachment, making observation of the latch the essential first step. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is considered a critical daily intervention to help prevent postpartum psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Stopping all forms of social interaction for six months
options.B: Encouraging her to stay awake all night to watch the newborn
options.C: Ensuring the mother gets uninterrupted blocks of sleep at night
options.D: Restricting her fluid intake during the first week after birth

explanation: Sleep deprivation is a potent trigger for postpartum mania and psychosis; protecting sleep is vital. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h7)

question: How do sebaceous glands release their oily product?

options.A: By pushing tiny droplets through the cell wall
options.B: By pumping fluid out using active transport
options.C: By bursting open and destroying the whole cell
options.D: By leaking slowly through open pores without cell loss

explanation: Holocrine secretion means the glandular cells fill up with oil and completely disintegrate to release their contents. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h2)

question: Which foods should you encourage for a patient healing from a broken bone?

options.A: High sodium and low potassium liquids
options.B: High protein, calcium, and Vitamin D
options.C: Strict water fasting for several days
options.D: Low fat, high sugar, and simple carbohydrates

explanation: Protein, calcium, and Vitamin D are essential building blocks for bone regeneration and tissue repair following a fracture. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T3#BMP216_U3_T3_h7)

question: How does Clostridium tetani typically enter the body during childbirth in low-resource community settings?

options.A: Through unsterile cord cutting tools
options.B: By direct skin-to-skin contact
options.C: Through contaminated drinking water
options.D: By breathing infected room air

explanation: Spores from soil or unclean instruments can contaminate the umbilical stump or genital tract during unhygienic delivery practices. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T8#BMP116_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is a key sign of lithium toxicity in a breastfed newborn?

options.A: Excessive production of thick saliva
options.B: Continuous high-pitched crying spells
options.C: Lethargy and poor muscle tone
options.D: Sudden rapid infant weight gain

explanation: Babies affected by too much lithium from breast milk often appear very floppy, sleepy, and feed poorly. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T3#BMP223_U4_T3_h6)

question: What shape does the pelvic inlet usually take in a platypelloid pelvis?

options.A: Heart-shaped or triangular
options.B: Long narrow funnel
options.C: Transverse oval or kidney-shaped
options.D: Round and symmetrical

explanation: The flattening of the inlet creates a broad, kidney-like or wide oval outline. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T6#BMP210_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is a classic sign of a thyroid storm (a severe, life-threatening flare-up of hyperthyroidism)?

options.A: Dangerously high fever
options.B: Marked hypothermia
options.C: Low resting heart rate
options.D: Slow, shallow breathing

explanation: Thyroid storm involves extreme hyperpyrexia, where body temperature climbs to dangerous levels alongside a very rapid heart rate. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T5#BMP216_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which reflex is routinely tested during antenatal checks to monitor for hypertensive disorders?

options.A: Triceps reflex
options.B: Achilles reflex
options.C: Biceps reflex
options.D: Patellar reflex

explanation: The knee-jerk or patellar reflex is the standard deep tendon reflex checked to monitor central nervous system irritability in pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T1#BMP110_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why is reading every word directly from the projection screen discouraged during a health talk?

options.A: Audience members read faster than the speaker talks, causing boredom
options.B: Projector bulbs burn out faster if text remains static for too long
options.C: PowerPoint software automatically penalizes speakers who read text
options.D: It is against the official copyright laws for medical presentations

explanation: Reading word-for-word makes the presentation monotonous and disconnects the speaker from the audience. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is physical cleaning with water and detergent mandatory BEFORE putting instruments into an autoclave?

options.A: Dried organic matter protects underlying microbes from steam penetration.
options.B: Water helps the autoclave heat up faster and saves electricity.
options.C: Soap makes the metal instruments look shiny and attractive to doctors.
options.D: Detergents are powerful enough to kill bacterial spores on their own.

explanation: If blood and tissue debris remain baked on the instrument, steam cannot reach the covered microbes, resulting in failed sterilization. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T1#BMP116_U5_T1_h6)

question: A postpartum woman develops sudden wheezing, low blood pressure, and widespread hives minutes after receiving an antibiotic injection. What is the most accurate clinical interpretation?

options.A: She is showing symptoms of normal postpartum hormonal shifts.
options.B: She is having a normal psychological reaction to the injection pain.
options.C: She is experiencing acute anaphylaxis affecting multiple body systems.
options.D: She has developed a mild side effect that requires simple reassurance.

explanation: The involvement of the skin, respiratory tract, and cardiovascular system simultaneously confirms a systemic anaphylactic shock event. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T7#BMP120_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is a major organizational advantage of using lectures for large classes?

options.A: It replaces all textbook reading with audio recordings
options.B: It accommodates many learners using only one instructor
options.C: It forces every student to perform a clinical delivery
options.D: It eliminates the need for any physical classroom space

explanation: The main strength of a lecture is that a single teacher can reach a large group of students all at once. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h3)

question: What helps a surgeon decide whether to repair the uterus or perform a hysterectomy?

options.A: The personal preference of the nurse on duty
options.B: The brand of suture material available in the theatre
options.C: The time of day the surgery takes place
options.D: The extent of the tear and the patient's desire for future children

explanation: Surgeons look at how severe the damage is and whether the mother still hopes to have more children when deciding how to proceed. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T4#BMP311_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why are fingernails useful beyond just protecting the fingers?

options.A: They help improve fine touch and picking up tiny items
options.B: They produce sweat to cool down the fingertips
options.C: They prevent bacteria from entering the bloodstream
options.D: They absorb extra vitamins produced by the hands

explanation: The counter-pressure from the nail plate against the finger pulp enhances the sensitivity of touch receptors. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T9#BMP111_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is the medical term for having a lower than normal number of platelets?

options.A: Thrombocytosis
options.B: Leukopenia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Erythrocytosis

explanation: Thrombocytopenia means low platelets, which can increase the risk of bleeding and easy bruising. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T4#BMP111_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why does a smaller, well-planned family often experience less domestic stress?

options.A: Parents never experience financial challenges regardless of economic conditions
options.B: Household chores are eliminated completely by modern appliances
options.C: Children do not require any medical attention as they grow up
options.D: Resources can be stretched less thinly to meet the basic needs of every member

explanation: When family size matches financial capacity, parents experience less anxiety over food, shelter, and school fees. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T1#BMP126_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why does a midwife check newborn reflexes and muscle tone during the first physical exam?

question: What is the primary purpose of assessing gestational age in a newborn?
